pezzi.0: Data and deterministic answers — Andrea Sforna AI
pezzi.1: The model does not touch the archive: it picks from operations that are already written and declared. Three possible outcomes, never mixed up with one another, and every number traces back to a read.

pezzi.5: Data and deterministic answers — Andrea Sforna AI
pezzi.6: The model does not touch the archive: it picks from operations that are already written and declared. Three possible outcomes, never mixed up with one another, and every number traces back to a read.
pezzi.35: The model picks, it does not read
pezzi.36: Between the model and the archive there is a set of operations written by hand. The model picks which one to call, and gets back what that operation actually read.
pezzi.38: Confusing the last two is the flaw that makes numbers get invented.
pezzi.43: It comes back as it is written in the archive, comparable with what was read.
pezzi.45: Declared absent. Not reconstructed, not estimated, not rounded.
pezzi.47: A visible error, never a plausible answer in place of a true one.
pezzi.48: A closed list, not free access
pezzi.49: Every operation has a name, parameters and a predictable result. Outside that list there is nothing to call: a question that matches no operation does not get an approximate answer.
pezzi.55: Traceable to the value that was read
pezzi.57: A number that is not in the database must not turn into a plausible number.
pezzi.59: Determinism holds inside the perimeter of the written operations. A question that falls outside does not get a better answer: it gets a refusal, and a new operation has to be added.
pezzi.62: Taking personal data out before the text reaches a model, and putting it back into the answer.
